title: Identity and composition for canonical derived étale cohomology pullback
statement: For schemes $X,Y,Z$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $f:Y\to X$ and $g:Z\to Y$. Let $K,L,N$ be bounded-below complexes of abelian etale sheaves on $X,Y,Z$, respectively [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Let $u:f^{-1}K\to L$ and $v:g^{-1}L\to N$ be complex morphisms [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Define $P_{f,u}^n:H^n(X,K)\to H^n(Y,L)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] as $H^n$ of the composite $R\Gamma_X(K)\xrightarrow{R\Gamma_X(\eta_f)}R\Gamma_X Rf_* f^{-1}K\xrightarrow{\lambda_f}R\Gamma_Y(f^{-1}K)\xrightarrow{R\Gamma_Y(u)}R\Gamma_Y(L)$, where $\lambda_f$ is the canonical Leray comparison. Under the inverse-image identity and composition isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition], $P_{\mathrm{id}_X,e_K}^n=\mathrm{id}$ and $P_{f\circ g,\,v\circ g^{-1}(u)\circ c^{-1}}^n=P_{g,v}^n\circ P_{f,u}^n$ for every integer $n$.

proof.text: For the identity, [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] identifies the unit followed by the direct-image identity and inverse-image identity comparisons with the identity. The Leray comparison is the derived global-section image of the direct-image comparison, by uniqueness of right-derived comparisons in [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Apply homology to obtain the identity law.

source.place: Lemma Tag 015J (lemma-two-ss-complex-functor), Remark Tag 015K; etale-cohomology.tex Lemma Tag 0EZM (lemma-colimit-variant-complexes)

proof.text: For composition, move the second unit past the first complex map by naturality. The composite-unit equation of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] turns these two units into the unit for the composite. The Leray comparisons agree with the derived direct-image composition comparison because they are induced by the same underived global-section comparisons; uniqueness of right-derived comparison transformations [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] gives their equality. Naturality of the complex-to-derived comparison combines u and v into v composed with g-inverse-image of u and the inverse of the inverse-image composition comparison. Apply global sections and homology, both of which preserve composition.
